about: The leaves of the network transcript that differ between two runs of ONE engine (the A/A of scripts/ci_ab_network.py). Each entry: `pattern` (fnmatch over the leaf path seeds/<seed>/<category>/...), `reason` (why that leaf is noise), `aa_run` (the A/A run that proved it). Born from the evidence of the A/A, never written ahead of it. It may only shrink: an entry that matches no leaf of a run is red as stale.

entries.reason: How many TCP connections the browser opens to each destination of the journey (the DoH, the two origins) is the connection pool's: parallel and speculative connections, keep-alive connections that close and reopen, DoH connections. The CONNECTs of the launch stage are counted with the journey ones (the DoH connection at start-up lands in either). The set of destinations and the order they were first reached stay compared (journey/connects/order). Totals of the two runs: Linux DoH 226 and 225, origin A 14 and 13, origin O 20 and 12; Windows DoH 222 and 230, A 23 and 15, O 22 and 14.
The connections to the DoH during the WebRTC page: 14 and 25 between the two Windows runs. Same pool; the destinations of the page (webrtc/connects/order) stay compared.

Whether a connection that resumes a session carried a request at all follows the ticket and the pool: an origin had one in a run and none in the other (seed 2 and seed 4 on Linux, h1: 108 leaves each), so what is under it is compared where both runs have a resumption and excused where only one has. The fresh connections (wire/connections) and the protocols stay compared always.
The same for the HTTP/3 site's resumed connection.

The engine sends an ECH extension with no real configuration (GREASE) and picks its AEAD at random for each ClientHello it builds, whether the handshake is fresh or resumed: NSS security/nss/lib/ssl/tls13ech.c:2257, `aead = (rawData->data[0] & 1) ? HpkeAeadAes128Gcm : HpkeAeadChaCha20Poly1305;` where rawData is HKDF output of a freshly generated key (tls13_MaybeGreaseEch, called from ssl3con.c:5888 for every ClientHello that has no real ECH, with or without a pre_shared_key). 1 (AES-128-GCM) or 3 (ChaCha20-Poly1305): Windows h2 first connection 1 then 3, h1 3 then 1, both values inside one run; resumed h1 connections 3 and 1 (seeds 2 and 4 on Windows, seed 63 on Linux). The rest of the extension (type, kdf, enc and payload lengths) stays compared.
The same ECH GREASE draw (tls13ech.c:2257) on the TLS connection of the HTTP/3 site (the HTTP/2 connection that opens before QUIC): 1 in one run and 3 in the other, on Linux and on Windows.
